title: Ringed image and factorization property of a quasi-compact flat monomorphism
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact flat monomorphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Here monomorphism means that postcomposition is injective on $\operatorname{Hom}(T,X)$ for every scheme $T$. Put $E=f(|X|)\subseteq|S|$ and give $E$ the subspace topology and inverse-image structure sheaf, so $S|_E=(E,\mathcal O_S|_E)$ is the ringed subspace [def-a1-ringed-subspace]. The morphism $f$ canonically identifies $X$ with $S|_E$ as a locally ringed space. The subset $E$ is stable under generalization (if $s\in E$ and $s\in\overline{\{t\}}$, then $t\in E$) and retrocompact (its intersection with every quasi-compact open of $S$ is quasi-compact). For any scheme $T$ and morphism $g:T\to S$, there is a unique morphism $a:T\to X$ with $f\circ a=g$ if and only if $g(|T|)\subseteq E$. Consequently two quasi-compact flat monomorphisms into $S$ with the same image are uniquely isomorphic over $S$. No finite-presentation, Noetherian or separation hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: §1 Propositions 1.1 and 1.2(i), Corollary 1.3, printed pp.1–2; generalization stability as used in Theorem 3.3 proof 1°. The factorization assertion is the immediate inverse-image-sheaf consequence of the canonical ringed-image identification, expanded in report.md; primary scan https://www.numdam.org/article/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf, read in sandbox sources/raynaud.pdf; project archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: First the monomorphism hypothesis gives an isomorphism $\Delta_f:X\to X\times_SX$: the two projections are equal by cancellation with $f$, and the diagonal and either projection are inverse by the fibre-product universal property. Apply [lem-per-flat-monomorphism-local-structure] to $f$ (with this diagonal isomorphism, flatness and quasi-compactness). It gives injectivity of $|f|$ and, for each $x\in X$, an isomorphism of the actual structural local ring maps $\mathcal O_{S,f(x)}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$. No finiteness or reducedness hypothesis is needed for these clauses.

source.place: Tag 01L6, lemma-monomorphism; Raynaud §1 Proposition 1.1 (online scan, printed p.1); the cited local-structure node supplies the local-ring assertion.

proof.text: Let $C\subseteq|X|$ be any closed subset. Choose a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with image $C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme]. The composite $h=f\circ i$ is quasi-compact: over an affine open $V\subseteq S$, its source is the closed subset $C\cap f^{-1}V$ of the quasi-compact space $f^{-1}V$; this is quasi-compact, by restricting an open cover and adjoining its open complement. Use [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and the closed-embedding clause of [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $F\hookrightarrow S$ be the scheme-theoretic image of $h$, supplied by [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc]. By [lem-sfb-scheme-image-flat-base-change], the closed subscheme $F\times_SX$ is the schematic image of $Z\times_SX\to X$. The map $Z\to Z\times_SX$ given by $(1_Z,i)$ is inverse to the first projection: for any compatible pair $(z,x)$, monicity of $f$ forces $x=i(z)$. Thus this base-changed map is $i$. Its schematic image is $Z$ by [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-of-closed-immersion]. Consequently $F\times_SX=Z$ as closed subschemes of $X$.

source.place: Tag 081I, lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image; Raynaud §1 Proposition 1.2(i), proof, printed p.2; existence of Z: schemes.tex Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme.

proof.text: The equality in Step 2 implies $f^{-1}(|F|)=C$. Indeed, on affine charts a pulled-back closed subscheme is cut out by the extended ideal, and a prime contains that ideal exactly when its inverse image contains the original ideal; this is the affine quotient description in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Injectivity of $f$ now gives $f(C)=E\cap|F|$. This is closed in $E$. The continuous bijection $\bar f:|X|\to E$ therefore carries every closed subset to a closed subset, so its inverse is continuous. Thus $\bar f$ is a homeomorphism for the subspace topology.

source.place: Tag 081I, conclusion of the schematic-image argument; Raynaud §1 Proposition 1.2(i), printed p.2, passage from inverse images of schematic images to the subspace topology.

proof.text: Let $\alpha:f^{-1}\mathcal O_S\to\mathcal O_X$ be the adjunct of the structure morphism, using [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. By [lem-pc-inverse-image-structure-stalk-iso], its stalk at $x$, preceded by the canonical ring isomorphism $\mathcal O_{S,f(x)}\cong(f^{-1}\mathcal O_S)_x$, is precisely $f_x^\sharp$. Step 1 makes this an isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheaf-iso-on-stalks] to the underlying sheaves of sets: the ring stalk is the same germ set, with operations on representatives over a common neighbourhood. Thus $\alpha$ is bijective on every open. Its inverse respects the ring operations since $\alpha$ does, and respects restrictions by composing the naturality square with the inverse component maps. Hence $\alpha$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings. Under the homeomorphism of Step 3, the inverse-image sheaf $f^{-1}\mathcal O_S$ is the transport of $i_E^{-1}\mathcal O_S$ to $X$: their neighbourhood diagrams are identified by $\bar f$, since $i_E\bar f=f$. By [def-a1-ringed-subspace], this identifies $X$ canonically with $S|_E$. Its stalks are the local rings $\mathcal O_{S,s}$, and the identified structural maps are local by [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. This is an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces over $S$.

source.place: Tags 008H (lemma-stalk-pullback), 007T (lemma-points-exactness), 008P (section-presheaves-structures-functorial); Raynaud §1 Proposition 1.2(i), final sentence of proof, printed p.2.

proof.text: For $s=f(x)\in E$ and $s\in\overline{\{t\}}$, the point $t$ specializes to $s$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-generalizations-lift] to obtain $x'$ specializing to $x$ with $f(x')=t$. Therefore $t\in E$. To prove retrocompactness, let $U\subseteq S$ be any quasi-compact open and choose a finite affine open cover $U=\bigcup_{j=1}^rV_j$. Each $f^{-1}V_j$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; their finite union $f^{-1}U$ is quasi-compact by the finite-subcover definition. Its continuous image $f(f^{-1}U)=E\cap U$ is quasi-compact: pull back any open cover, take a finite subcover of the source, then map back. This also covers $U=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 03HV, lemma-generalizations-lift-flat; quasi-compactness definition (Tag 01K2) and Raynaud §1 Definition 1.4, printed pp.2–3.

proof.text: Let $g:T\to S$ have image contained in $E$. The map $b:T\to E$ obtained by restricting the codomain of $g$ is continuous, because the inverse image of $E\cap V$, for $V$ open in $S$, is $g^{-1}V$. Therefore $a_0=\bar f^{-1}\circ b:|T|\to|X|$ is continuous and satisfies $f\circ a_0=|g|$. All stalk maps of $f$ are isomorphisms by Step 1, so [new-lem-zl-stalk-isomorphism-lifting], with its $W=T$ and $Y=S$, supplies a scheme morphism $a:T\to X$ having this underlying map and $f\circ a=g$. Any two such morphisms are equal by the original monomorphism hypothesis. Conversely $g=f\circ a$ immediately gives $g(|T|)\subseteq f(|X|)=E$.

source.place: Tags 008C (section-presheaves-functorial), 008P (section-presheaves-structures-functorial), 0091 (definition-ringed-space): inverse-image sheaf mapping property, as packaged in the cited lifting node; this expands the ringed-image consequence of Raynaud §1 Proposition 1.2(i).

proof.text: Finally let $f_j:X_j\to S$ ($j=1,2$) satisfy the hypotheses and have the same image $E$. Apply Step 6 to $g=f_2$ and $f=f_1$, and then with the indices exchanged, to obtain unique $S$-morphisms $u:X_2\to X_1$ and $v:X_1\to X_2$. Since $f_1uv=f_1$ and $f_2vu=f_2$, monicity gives $uv=1_{X_1}$ and $vu=1_{X_2}$. Thus $u$ is the unique isomorphism over $S$. Every preceding argument used only quasi-compactness, flatness and monicity, as required.
